newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds stable as buyer interest fizzles.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds stable as buyer interest fizzles.

text.p: Argentine bonds were stable-to-lower late Tuesday as an early rise fizzled out on a lack of follow-through buying.
"Investors are waiting for the U.S. economic indicators later this week before entering the market," said a trader at a foreign bank.
Argentina's FRB due 2005 fell 1/8 to 83-6/8, while the local dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 2 due 2001 was stable at 120.00.
Trade was busy in the morning but slowed during the afternoon, said traders.
Another trader said "the yields on local bonds are attractive, something which should attract capital from overseas. There was more movement than in previous days."
Traders said the monthly auction of treasury bills this session did not have much impact, although yields on the issues were higher than at the last auction.
The Economy Ministry placed 250 million pesos in 91-day treasury bills at a cut-off yield of 7.60 percent and another $250 million in 182-day bills at 7.60 percent.
At last month's auction of 91-day peso bills there was a cut-off yield of 7.21 percent. The last time 182-day dollar bills were issued was in August, when there was a cut-off yield of 6.49 percent.
In the money markets, call money rose to 7.03 percent from 6.93 percent.
